scenario: A museum-curation residency admits applicants if they have either elite exhibition-design skill or elite conservation-science skill. A 5% wildcard also admits candidates with neither trait. Reviewers think design and conservation skill are negatively related among residents.

data.description: Admission is based on either trait plus a wildcard.

question: Among admitted residents, compute (a) P(design | conservation, selected), and (b) P(design | not conservation, selected). Is the negative association real or a selection artifact?

ground_truth.explanation: The residency rule induces collider bias even if the traits are independent in the applicant pool.

naive_answer: Design and conservation skill appear negatively related among residents, so the abilities probably substitute.
naive_trap: Conditioning on admission creates a spurious negative association.
